title: The deliberate buy accepts any positive amount and applies none of the bot buy guards except affordability (no risk gate: max position size, open positions, exposure, cooldown, daily loss; no circuit breaker; no pause); the only stop before signing is a 5-second "press Ctrl+C" window, which may not stop an npx-launched script on Windows

evidence.note: amountEth is parsed with parseEther and only checked to be > 0; no upper bound, no comparison with the configured snipe amount or caps
banner (chain, wallet, balance, token, dex, value) and "Aborting in 5s - press Ctrl+C now", then sleep(5000) and sign; no typed confirmation
executeDeliberateBuy runs enforceEntryExitAffordability and then signs; canSnipe (the risk gate imported at :109) is not called on this path
import { canSnipe, recordSnipe } from ./riskManager: used by the snipe handlers only

sibling_sites_checked: All callers of executeDeliberateBuy at the base (git grep: scripts/deliberate-buy.ts:142 only). The snipe handlers call the risk gate and the pause checkpoints; the deliberate path calls neither. Other signing scripts have no confirmation step at all (recover-sell-ladys.ts signs right after printing the quote; AUD-SCRIPTS-003).
severity_rationale: S2. The operator types the amount and the banner prints it, so an overspend needs both a mistake (for example 1 instead of 0.1) and a missed banner; the wallet balance and the affordability gate bound it. The bypassed caps are mostly unset or not enforced today (MAX_POSITION_SIZE has no default, TH-DB-03; per-chain max capital is not a cap, AUD-DB-014), so the bypass matters most once Phase 24 enforces them. The Ctrl+C part is recorded as unverified (sub_claims).
recommendation: Decide on card SCRIPTS-02 which bot guards a deliberate buy must pass (risk gate, circuit breaker, pause) and how the operator confirms before signing (typed confirmation of chain, token and amount instead of a timed Ctrl+C window, or both). Phase 23 should prove on the operator terminal (Git Bash, npx ts-node) whether Ctrl+C during the window actually stops the script before signing.

sub_claims.claim: No risk gate, circuit breaker or pause check on the deliberate buy path
No upper bound on the amount

Ctrl+C during the 5-second window may not stop the script when launched through npx in Git Bash on Windows (the operator-recorded note in STATE.md says npx swallows Ctrl+C there, which is why the bot is stopped by killing the PID)
sub_claims.status: unverified: environment behaviour; prove in Phase 23 without signing (for example with a stub that only sleeps)
